{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_55970597ca9e4dff82324352","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t![NEEDLE](docs/hero.png)\n2\t\n3\t# 🧵 NEEDLE\n4\t\n5\t[![CI](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\n6\t[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)\n7\t[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](rust-toolchain.toml)\n8\t[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.2.8-green.svg)](Cargo.toml)\n9\t\n10\t**N**avigates **E**very **E**nqueued **D**eliverable, **L**ogs **E**ffort\n11\t\n12\t> Deterministic bead processing with explicit outcome paths.\n13\t\n14\tNEEDLE is a universal wrapper for headless coding CLI agents. It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\n15\t\n16\t---\n17\t\n18\t## 🚀 Quickstart\n19\t\n20\t```bash\n21\t# Install the latest release\n22\tcurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\n23\t\n24\t# Or build from source\n25\tcargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\n26\t\n27\t# Run a worker against a bead-tracked workspace\n28\tcd /path/to/your/workspace\n29\tneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\n30\t```\n31\t\n32\tA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\n33\t\n34\tSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\n35\t\n36\t---\n37\t\n38\t## 🧶 What is a bead?\n39\t\n40\tA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\n41\t\n42\tBeads live in a **bead store** — a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a JSONL checkpoint file (`issues.jsonl`) in a `.beads/` directory inside your project. The `br` CLI manages the bead store: create beads, list them, claim them, close them.\n43\t\n44\t```bash\n45\t# Create a bead\n46\tbr create --title \"Add pagination to search results\" --body \"...\"\n47\t\n48\t# List open beads\n49\tbr list --status open\n50\t\n51\t# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\n52\t```\n53\t\n54\tNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\n55\t\n56\t---\n57\t\n58\t## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\n59\t\n60\tExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\n61\t\n62\t- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\n63\t- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\n64\t\n65\tNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\n66\t\n67\t---\n68\t\n69\t## 🧠 Core Principle\n70\t\n71\tNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\n72\t\n73\t```\n74\tIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\n75\tIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\n76\t```\n77\t\n78\t---\n79\t\n80\t## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\n81\t\n82\tA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\n83\t\n84\t```\n85\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n86\t│                                                     │\n87\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n88\t│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\n89\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\n90\t│         │                                        │  │\n91\t│         ▼                                        │  │\n92\t│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │\n93\t│   │  🔒 CLAIM  │──────────────►│ 🔁 RETRY  │─────┘  │\n94\t│   └─────┬─────┘               └──────────┘        │\n95\t│         │ claimed                                   │\n96\t│         ▼                                           │\n97\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n98\t│   │ 📋 BUILD   │                                     │\n99\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n100\t│         │                                           │\n101\t│         ▼                                           │\n102\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n103\t│   │ 🚀 DISPATCH│                                     │\n104\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n105\t│         │                                           │\n106\t│         ▼                                           │\n107\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n108\t│   │ ⏳ EXECUTE │                                     │\n109\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n110\t│         │                                           │\n111\t│         ▼                                           │\n112\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n113\t│   │ 📊 OUTCOME │                                     │\n114\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n115\t│         │                                           │\n116\t│         ├── ✅ success ──► close bead ──────────────┘\n117\t│         ├── ❌ failure ──► log + release ────────────┘\n118\t│         ├── ⏰ timeout ──► release + defer ──────────┘\n119\t│         └── 💀 crash ────► release + alert ──────────┘\n120\t│                                                     │\n121\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n122\t```\n123\t\n124\t---\n125\t\n126\t## 📐 Algorithm Steps\n127\t\n128\t### 🔍 Step 1: Select\n129\t\n130\tQuery the bead queue for the next claimable bead in **deterministic priority order**. Selection is not random — given the same queue state, every worker computes the same ordering. Ties are broken by creation time (oldest first).\n131\t\n132\t### 🔒 Step 2: Claim\n133\t\n134\tAttempt an **atomic claim** via `br update --claim`. SQLite transaction isolation guarantees exactly one worker succeeds. If the claim fails (race lost), return to Step 1 with the losing candidate excluded.\n135\t\n136\t### 📋 Step 3: Build\n137\t\n138\tConstruct the prompt from the bead's context: title, body, workspace path, relevant files, and any dependency context. The prompt is a deterministic function of the bead state — same bead, same prompt.\n139\t\n140\t### 🚀 Step 4: Dispatch\n141\t\n142\tLoad the agent adapter configuration (YAML), render the invoke template with the built prompt, and execute via `bash -c`. The agent runs headless — it receives a prompt, does work, and exits.\n143\t\n144\t### ⏳ Step 5: Execute\n145\t\n146\tThe agent runs. NEEDLE waits. The only inputs are the exit code and stdout/stderr. There is no interactive communication during execution.\n147\t\n148\t### 📊 Step 6: Outcome\n149\t\n150\tEvaluate the result and follow the **explicit path** for the observed outcome:\n151\t\n152\t| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler |\n153\t|---------|-----------|---------|\n154\t| ✅ **Success** | `0` | Validate output → close bead → log effort → **loop** |\n155\t| ❌ **Failure** | `1` | Log failure reason → release bead → increment retry count → **loop** |\n156\t| ⏰ **Timeout** | `124` | Release bead → mark deferred → **loop** |\n157\t| 💀 **Crash** | `>128` | Release bead → create alert bead → **loop** |\n158\t| 🏁 **Race Lost** | `4` | (Handled at Step 2) → exclude candidate → **retry select** |\n159\t| 🫙 **Queue Empty** | — | Enter strand escalation → **explore / mend / knot** |\n160\t\n161\tEvery row is implemented. There are no unhandled cases.\n162\t\n163\t---\n164\t\n165\t## 🧶 Strand Escalation\n166\t\n167\tWhen the primary workspace has no claimable beads, NEEDLE follows a **strand sequence** to find or create work. Each strand is evaluated in order — the first strand that yields a bead wins.\n168\t\n169\t| # | Strand | Agent? | Purpose |\n170\t|---|--------|--------|---------|\n171\t| 1 | 🪡 **Pluck** | Yes | Process beads from the assigned workspace |\n172\t| 2 | 🔭 **Explore** | No | Search other workspaces for claimable beads |\n173\t| 3 | 🔧 **Mend** | No | Cleanup: orphaned claims, stale locks, health checks |\n174\t| 4 | 🕸️ **Weave** | Yes | Create beads from documentation gaps *(opt-in)* |\n175\t| 5 | 🪢 **Unravel** | Yes | Propose alternatives for HUMAN-blocked beads *(opt-in)* |\n176\t| 6 | 💓 **Pulse** | Yes | Codebase health scans, auto-generate beads *(opt-in)* |\n177\t| 7 | 🪢 **Knot** | No | All strands exhausted — alert human, wait |\n178\t\n179\t---\n180\t\n181\t## ⚡ Parallel Workers\n182\t\n183\tMultiple NEEDLE workers run independently with **no central orchestrator**. Coordination happens through the shared bead queue:\n184\t\n185\t- **Atomicity** — `br update --claim` uses SQLite transactions; exactly one worker wins each claim\n186\t- **Determinism** — all workers compute the same priority order; races are resolved by the database, not by timing\n187\t- **Independence** — each worker is a self-contained loop in its own tmux session\n188\t- **Naming** — workers use NATO alphabet identifiers: `alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, ...\n189\t\n190\t```\n191\t  needle-claude-sonnet-alpha ──┐\n192\t  needle-claude-sonnet-bravo ──┤\n193\t  needle-codex-gpt4-charlie ───┼──► Shared .beads/ (SQLite + JSONL)\n194\t  needle-opencode-qwen-delta ──┤\n195\t  needle-aider-sonnet-echo ────┘\n196\t```\n197\t\n198\t---\n199\t\n200\t## 🏗️ Supported Agents\n201\t\n202\tNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. Any CLI that accepts a prompt and exits works.\n203\t\n204\t| Agent | CLI | Input Method | Notes |\n205\t|-------|-----|-------------|-------|\n206\t| Claude Code (interactive) | `claude-interactive` | stdin | **Recommended** — uses subscription billing; see [plugin](#-claude-interactive-plugin) |\n207\t| Claude Code (API) | `claude --print` | stdin | Uses programmatic/API billing |\n208\t| OpenCode | `opencode` | file | |\n209\t| Codex CLI | `codex` | args | |\n210\t| Aider | `aider --message` | args | |\n211\t| *Custom* | *any* | *configurable via YAML adapter* | |\n212\t\n213\tAdding a new agent requires **only a YAML configuration file** — no code changes.\n214\t\n215\t---\n216\t\n217\t## 🔌 claude-interactive Plugin\n218\t\n219\tThe `claude-interactive` plugin ships as a separate release asset. It wraps the Claude Code CLI in a PTY so workers run under your **Claude subscription** instead of consuming programmatic API credits.\n220\t\n221\t**How it works:** NEEDLE pipes subprocess stdio, which causes `claude` to detect a non-TTY and switch to API billing. `claude-interactive` creates an internal PTY so `claude` sees a real terminal, keeping it in interactive/subscription mode.\n222\t\n223\t**Install:**\n224\t\n225\t```bash\n226\tgh release download v0.2.6 --repo jedarden/NEEDLE --pattern 'claude-interactive*'\n227\tchmod +x claude-interactive-install.sh\n228\t./claude-interactive-install.sh\n229\t```\n230\t\n231\t**Requirements:** Python 3.10+, `pyte` (`pip install pyte`), and the `claude` CLI on PATH.\n232\t\n233\t**Run:**\n234\t\n235\t```bash\n236\tcd /path/to/workspace\n237\tneedle run --agent claude-interactive --count 4\n238\t```\n239\t\n240\tSource lives in [`plugins/claude-interactive/`](plugins/claude-interactive/).\n241\t\n242\t---\n243\t\n244\t## 📁 Repository Structure\n245\t\n246\t```\n247\tNEEDLE/\n248\t├── Cargo.toml             # Rust crate manifest\n249\t├── install.sh             # One-line installer for prebuilt binaries\n250\t├── plugins/\n251\t│   └── claude-interactive/ # PTY wrapper — subscription billing adapter for Claude Code\n252\t├── src/\n253\t│   ├── main.rs            # Worker entry point\n254\t│   ├── lib.rs             # Library root\n255\t│   ├── claim/             # Atomic bead claiming via SQLite transactions\n256\t│   ├── dispatch/          # Agent invocation + YAML adapter loading\n257\t│   ├── outcome/           # Explicit handler per outcome type\n258\t│   ├── strand/            # Pluck / Explore / Mend / Weave / Knot logic\n259\t│   ├── decision/          # Outcome classification from agent exit + output\n260\t│   ├── peer/              # Multi-worker coordination, peer discovery\n261\t│   ├── mitosis/           # Worker spawn / lifecycle / supervised respawn\n262\t│   ├── health/            # Liveness, stale-claim cleanup, watchdog\n263\t│   ├── learning/          # Per-agent performance tracking and weighting\n264\t│   ├── telemetry/         # OTLP exporter, gen_ai semantic conventions\n265\t│   ├── trace/             # Span construction for state transitions\n266\t│   ├── cost/              # It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\n\n---\n\n## 🚀 Quickstart\n\n```bash\n# Install the latest release\ncurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\n\n# Or build from source\ncargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\n\n# Run a worker against a bead-tracked workspace\ncd /path/to/your/workspace\nneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\n```\n\nA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\n\nSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\n\n---\n\n## 🧶 What is a bead?\n\nA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\n\nBeads live in a **bead store** — a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a JSONL checkpoint file (`issues.jsonl`) in a `.beads/` directory inside your project. The `br` CLI manages the bead store: create beads, list them, claim them, close them.\n\n```bash\n# Create a bead\nbr create --title \"Add pagination to search results\" --body \"...\"\n\n# List open beads\nbr list --status open\n\n# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\n```\n\nNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\n\n---\n\n## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\n\nExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\n\n- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\n- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\n\nNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\n\n---\n\n## 🧠 Core Principle\n\nNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\n\n```\nIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\nIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\n```\n\n---\n\n## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\n\nA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                     │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\n│         │                                        │  │\n│         ▼                                        │  │\n│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │\n│   │  🔒 CLAIM  │──────────────►│ 🔁 RETRY  │─────┘  │\n│   └─────┬─────┘               └──────────┘        │\n│         │ claimed                                   │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ 📋 BUILD   │                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ 🚀 DISPATCH│                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ ⏳ EXECUTE │                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ 📊 OUTCOME │                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ├── ✅ success ──► close bead ──────────────┘\n│         ├── ❌ failure ──► log + release ────────────┘\n│         ├── ⏰ timeout ──► release + defer ──────────┘\n│         └── 💀 crash ────► release + alert ──────────┘\n│                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 📐 Algorithm Steps\n\n### 🔍 Step 1: Select\n\nQuery the bead queue for the next claimable bead in **deterministic priority order**. Selection is not random — given the same queue state, every worker computes the same ordering. Ties are broken by creation time (oldest first).\n\n### 🔒 Step 2: Claim\n\nAttempt an **atomic claim** via `br update --claim`. SQLite transaction isolation guarantees exactly one worker succeeds. If the claim fails (race lost), return to Step 1 with the losing candidate excluded.\n\n### 📋 Step 3: Build\n\nConstruct the prompt from the bead's context: title, body, workspace path, relevant files, and any dependency context. The prompt is a deterministic function of the bead state — same bead, same prompt.\n\n### 🚀 Step 4: Dispatch\n\nLoad the agent adapter configuration (YAML), render the invoke template with the built prompt, and execute via `bash -c`. The agent runs headless — it receives a prompt, does work, and exits.\n\n### ⏳ Step 5: Execute\n\nThe agent runs. NEEDLE waits. The only inputs are the exit code and stdout/stderr. There is no interactive communication during execution.\n\n### 📊 Step 6: Outcome\n\nEvaluate the result and follow the **explicit path** for the observed outcome:\n\n| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler |\n|---------|-----------|---------|\n| ✅ **Success** | `0` | Validate output → close bead → log effort → **loop** |\n| ❌ **Failure** | `1` | Log failure reason → release bead → increment retry count → **loop** |\n| ⏰ **Timeout** | `124` | Release bead → mark deferred → **loop** |\n| 💀 **Crash** | `>128` | Release bead → create alert bead → **loop** |\n| 🏁 **Race Lost** | `4` | (Handled at Step 2) → exclude candidate → **retry select** |\n| 🫙 **Queue Empty** | — | Enter strand escalation → **explore / mend / knot** |\n\nEvery row is implemented. There are no unhandled cases.\n\n---\n\n## 🧶 Strand Escalation\n\nWhen the primary workspace has no claimable beads, NEEDLE follows a **strand sequence** to find or create work. Each strand is evaluated in order — the first strand that yields a bead wins.\n\n| # | Strand | Agent? | Purpose |\n|---|--------|--------|---------|\n| 1 | 🪡 **Pluck** | Yes | Process beads from the assigned workspace |\n| 2 | 🔭 **Explore** | No | Search other workspaces for claimable beads |\n| 3 | 🔧 **Mend** | No | Cleanup: orphaned claims, stale locks, health checks |\n| 4 | 🕸️ **Weave** | Yes | Create beads from documentation gaps *(opt-in)* |\n| 5 | 🪢 **Unravel** | Yes | Propose alternatives for HUMAN-blocked beads *(opt-in)* |\n| 6 | 💓 **Pulse** | Yes | Codebase health scans, auto-generate beads *(opt-in)* |\n| 7 | 🪢 **Knot** | No | All strands exhausted — alert human, wait |\n\n---\n\n## ⚡ Parallel Workers\n\nMultiple NEEDLE workers run independently with **no central orchestrator**. Coordination happens through the shared bead queue:\n\n- **Atomicity** — `br update --claim` uses SQLite transactions; exactly one worker wins each claim\n- **Determinism** — all workers compute the same priority order; races are resolved by the database, not by timing\n- **Independence** — each worker is a self-contained loop in its own tmux session\n- **Naming** — workers use NATO alphabet identifiers: `alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, ...\n\n```\n  needle-claude-sonnet-alpha ──┐\n  needle-claude-sonnet-bravo ──┤\n  needle-codex-gpt4-charlie ───┼──► Shared .beads/ (SQLite + JSONL)\n  needle-opencode-qwen-delta ──┤\n  needle-aider-sonnet-echo ────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 🏗️ Supported Agents\n\nNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. Any CLI that accepts a prompt and exits works.\n\n| Agent | CLI | Input Method | Notes |\n|-------|-----|-------------|-------|\n| Claude Code (interactive) | `claude-interactive` | stdin | **Recommended** — uses subscription billing; see [plugin](#-claude-interactive-plugin) |\n| Claude Code (API) | `claude --print` | stdin | Uses programmatic/API billing |\n| OpenCode | `opencode` | file | |\n| Codex CLI | `codex` | args | |\n| Aider | `aider --message` | args | |\n| *Custom* | *any* | *configurable via YAML adapter* | |\n\nAdding a new agent requires **only a YAML configuration file** — no code changes.\n\n---\n\n## 🔌 claude-interactive Plugin\n\nThe `claude-interactive` plugin ships as a separate release asset. It wraps the Claude Code CLI in a PTY so workers run under your **Claude subscription** instead of consuming programmatic API credits.\n\n**How it works:** NEEDLE pipes subprocess stdio, which causes `claude` to detect a non-TTY and switch to API billing. `claude-interactive` creates an internal PTY so `claude` sees a real terminal, keeping it in interactive/subscription mode.\n\n**Install:**\n\n```bash\ngh release download v0.2.6 --repo jedarden/NEEDLE --pattern 'claude-interactive*'\nchmod +x claude-interactive-install.sh\n./claude-interactive-install.sh\n```\n\n**Requirements:** Python 3.10+, `pyte` (`pip install pyte`), and the `claude` CLI on PATH.\n\n**Run:**\n\n```bash\ncd /path/to/workspace\nneedle run --agent claude-interactive --count 4\n```\n\nSource lives in [`plugins/claude-interactive/`](plugins/claude-interactive/).\n\n---\n\n## 📁 Repository Structure\n\n```\nNEEDLE/\n├── Cargo.toml             # Rust crate manifest\n├── install.sh             # One-line installer for prebuilt binaries\n├── plugins/\n│   └── claude-interactive/ # PTY wrapper — subscription billing adapter for Claude Code\n├── src/\n│   ├── main.rs            # Worker entry point\n│   ├── lib.rs             # Library root\n│   ├── claim/             # Atomic bead claiming via SQLite transactions\n│   ├── dispatch/          # Agent invocation + YAML adapter loading\n│   ├── outcome/           # Explicit handler per outcome type\n│   ├── strand/            # Pluck / Explore / Mend / Weave / Knot logic\n│   ├── decision/          # Outcome classification from agent exit + output\n│   ├── peer/              # Multi-worker coordination, peer discovery\n│   ├── mitosis/           # Worker spawn / lifecycle / supervised respawn\n│   ├── health/            # Liveness, stale-claim cleanup, watchdog\n│   ├── learning/          # Per-agent performance tracking and weighting\n│   ├── telemetry/         # OTLP exporter, gen_ai semantic conventions\n│   ├── trace/             # Span construction for state transitions\n│   ├── cost/              # Token + USD spend tracking per bead and worker\n│   ├── rate_limit/        # Quota enforcement, backoff, weekly limit gates\n│   ├── prompt/            # Deterministic prompt construction from bead\n│   ├── registry/          # Agent adapter registry (YAML-loaded)\n│   ├── sanitize/          # Output redaction and prompt-injection guards\n│   ├── validation/        # Pre-dispatch and post-execution checks\n│   ├── worker/            # Worker session and identity management\n│   ├── config/            # `.needle.yaml` parsing and defaults\n│   └── bin/               # Auxiliary binaries (transform helpers)\n├── tests/                 # Integration tests\n├── ci/                    # Docker images used by GitHub Actions\n├── .github/workflows/     # CI + release pipelines\n├── config/                # Default agent adapters\n└── docs/                  # Plan, research, examples, post-mortems\n```\n\n---\n\n## 🔍 Observability\n\nNEEDLE emits structured telemetry for every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome. A silent worker is a broken worker.\n\n### Exported Signals\n\n| Signal | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| **Traces** | Spans for `worker.session`, `bead.lifecycle`, `bead.claim`, `agent.dispatch`, `strand.evaluated`, `outcome.handled` |\n| **Metrics** | `needle.beads.completed`, `needle.beads.duration`, `needle.agent.tokens.input`, `needle.cost.usd`, and more |\n| **Logs** | All events not represented as spans, with severity mapping (`ERROR` for failures, `WARN` for stale peers) |\n\n### OpenTelemetry (OTLP) Export\n\nNEEDLE can export telemetry to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, etc.) via OTLP.\n\n**Minimal configuration (`.needle.yaml`):**\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  otlp_sink:\n    enabled: true\n    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"  # gRPC, or :4318 for HTTP\n    protocol: \"grpc\"\n```\n\n**Semantic conventions:** NEEDLE follows OpenTelemetry's `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions for LLM telemetry, enabling out-of-the-box integration with GenAI dashboards (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).\n\nSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) for the complete semantic mapping table.\n\n---\n\n## 📊 Production Status\n\nNEEDLE currently powers my own headless multi-agent workflow — workers run continuously against shared bead queues, dispatching to Claude Code and other CLIs, with full OTLP telemetry wired through. Pluck strand: primary bead selection from the assigned workspace.\n//!\n//! Pluck handles >90% of all bead processing. It queries the bead store for\n//! unassigned, ready beads, filters by excluded labels, and sorts them in\n//! deterministic priority order: `(priority ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC)`.\n//!\n//! Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same candidate list.\n\nuse crate::bead_store::{BeadStore, Filters};\nuse crate::types::{Bead, StrandError, StrandResult};\n\n/// Default labels excluded from Pluck selection when not configured.\nconst DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_LABELS: &[&str] = &[\"deferred\", \"human\", \"blocked\", \"starvation-alert\"];\n\n/// The Pluck strand — primary work selection.\npub struct PluckStrand {\n    /// Labels to exclude from candidate selection.\n    exclude_labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Auto-split beads after this many consecutive failures (0 = disabled).\n    split_after_failures: u32,\n}\n\nimpl PluckStrand {\n    /// Create a new PluckStrand with the given exclude labels.\n    ///\n    /// If `exclude_labels` is empty, the default set (`deferred`, `human`,\n    /// `blocked`) is used.\n    pub fn new(exclude_labels: Vec<String>) -> Self {\n        let labels = if exclude_labels.is_empty() {\n            DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_LABELS\n                .iter()\n                .map(|s| (*s).to_string())\n                .collect()\n        } else {\n            exclude_labels\n        };\n        PluckStrand {\n            exclude_labels: labels,\n            split_after_failures: 3, // default threshold\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new PluckStrand with the given exclude labels and split threshold.\n    ///\n    /// If `exclude_labels` is empty, the default set (`deferred`, `human`,\n    /// `blocked`) is used.\n    pub fn with_split_threshold(exclude_labels: Vec<String>, split_after_failures: u32) -> Self {\n        let labels = if exclude_labels.is_empty() {\n            DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_LABELS\n                .iter()\n                .map(|s| (*s).to_string())\n                .collect()\n        } else {\n            exclude_labels\n        };\n        PluckStrand {\n            exclude_labels: labels,\n            split_after_failures,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Extract the failure count from a bead's labels.\n    ///\n    /// Labels follow the pattern `failure-count:N`. Returns the count if found,\n    /// or 0 if no failure-count label exists.\n    fn extract_failure_count(bead: &Bead) -> u32 {\n        bead.labels\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"failure-count:\"))\n            .filter_map(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Sort candidates in deterministic priority order.\n    ///\n    /// Sort key: `(priority ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC)`.\n    /// The id tie-breaker ensures identical ordering across platforms.\n    fn sort_candidates(candidates: &mut [Bead]) {\n        candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            a.priority\n                .cmp(&b.priority)\n                .then_with(|| a.created_at.cmp(&b.created_at))\n                .then_with(|| a.id.as_ref().cmp(b.id.as_ref()))\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl super::Strand for PluckStrand {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"pluck\"\n    }\n\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"strand.pluck\",\n        skip(self, store),\n        fields(\n            strand = \"pluck\",\n            exclude_labels = ?self.exclude_labels,\n        )\n    )]\n    async fn evaluate(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore) -> StrandResult {\n        // 1. Query bead store for ready, unassigned beads.\n        let filters = Filters {\n            assignee: None,\n            exclude_labels: self.exclude_labels.clone(),\n        };\n\n        let mut candidates = match store.ready(&filters).await {\n            Ok(beads) => beads,\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Bead store error is semantically different from NoWork.\n                return StrandResult::Error(StrandError::StoreError(e));\n            }\n        };\n\n        // 2. Filter: remove beads with excluded labels.\n        //    Defensive guard — store.ready() passes exclude_labels in its Filters,\n        //    but the backing CLI may not include label data in every query type.\n        //    Filtering here guarantees excluded-label beads are never presented as\n        //    candidates regardless of backend behaviour, preventing the\n        //    SELECTING→CLAIMING→RETRYING spin loop observed when br ready --json\n        //    omits label fields for some beads.\n        candidates.retain(|b| !b.labels.iter().any(|l| self.exclude_labels.contains(l)));\n\n        // 3. Filter: remove beads that are actively in_progress (claimed by another worker)\n        //    and Open beads with a stale assignee. These are never claimable — the claimer\n        //    will reject them every time, causing a hot loop.\n        candidates.retain(|b| {\n            !(matches!(b.status, crate::types::BeadStatus::InProgress)\n                || (b.status == crate::types::BeadStatus::Open && b.assignee.is_some()))\n        });\n\n        // 4. Sort: deterministic (priority, created_at, id).\n        Self::sort_candidates(&mut candidates);\n\n        // 5. Check for split trigger: if the first candidate has accumulated\n        //    enough consecutive failures, dispatch a SPLIT instruction instead\n        //    of returning the bead for normal processing.\n        if self.split_after_failures > 0 {\n            if let Some(first_candidate) = candidates.first() {\n                let failure_count = Self::extract_failure_count(first_candidate);\n                if failure_count >= self.split_after_failures {\n                    return StrandResult::Split(Box::new(first_candidate.clone()), failure_count);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 6. Return result.\n        if candidates.is_empty() {\n            StrandResult::NoWork\n        } else {\n            StrandResult::BeadFound(candidates)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests
